stories.headline: Earthquake of magnitude 6.1 strikes off Kanto coast, tsunami forecast issued for slight sea level changes
stories.title: Earthquake of magnitude 6.1 strikes off Kanto coast, tsunami forecast issued for slight sea level changes
stories.summary: New Delhi [India], November 6 : An earthquake measuring 6.1 on the Richter scale struck the North Pacific Ocean, off the eastern coast of the Kanto region, on Friday afternoon, according to the National Centre for Seismology (NCS). The seismic event was recorded at 4:09 PM IST on Friday, about 145 km from Choshi, Chiba, Japan. According to data released by the NCS, the earthquake originated at a relatively shallow depth of 40 kilometres beneath the surface. The epicentre of the tremor was located at latitude 35.087° N and longitude 142.254° E. "EQ of M: 6.1, On: 06/11/2026 16:09:29 IST, Lat: 35.087 N, Long: 142.254 E, Depth: 40 Km, Location: North Pacific Ocean," NCS posted on X. Meanwhile, the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) has issued a tsunami forecast following the earthquake off the eastern coast of the Kanto region. While no major tsunami warning, tsunami warning, or tsunami advisory has been triggered, the JMA’s forecast highlights potential minor sea-level fluctuations along the eastern Kanto coastline. Authorities do not expect destructive waves, but coastal residents and maritime operators are urged to remain attentive and follow official updates. Further details regarding potential impacts, felt intensities, or damage are currently awaited. Earlier in August, an earthquake with a magnitude of 6.0 struck parts of the northern Japanese prefecture of Hokkaido on Sunday evening, according to the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA), making it the second quake that hit Japan today. The epicentre of the quake was recorded off Hokkaido at a depth of 40 kilometres at 10:45 pm (local time). The seismic intensity scale was 4 out of a maximum of 7, as per JMA, which said that no tsunami warning was issued. Earlier this morning, an earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 5.9 hit the eastern region of the country, leaving over 40 people injured in Tokyo and neighbouring prefectures, authorities said, as per the official Kyodo News Agency. The tremor prompted a warning by the weather agency about similar quakes in the coming days. The 2:00 am (local time) quake had originated in the southern part of Ibaraki Prefecture at a depth of 68 kilometres and registered lower 5 on the Japanese seismic intensity scale of 7 in parts of the prefecture as well as in central Tokyo, the official media said. The morning quake was felt across a wide swath of the country, including northeastern and central Japan. The earthquake triggered delays for early morning train operations, while several services were compelled to proceed at reduced speeds, according to JR East and regional transit operators. According to the recorded parameters, the epicentre was located approximately 125 kilometres south of Obihiro and 36 kilometres south-southeast of Urakawa. Local authorities are monitoring the situation following the seismic event. Kyodo News noted that a lower 5 quake is defined by the agency as shaking that causes most people to be frightened and to hold on to something stable, while objects may fall from shelves. In the morning quake, transportation was impacted following the event. The start of some train services was delayed, while some trains ran at reduced speeds, according to JR East and other operators, as cited by Kyodo News. Furthermore, some express services operated by Tobu Railway remained halted. Following the early morning earthquake, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi announced that the government has established an emergency response task force at the PMO to assess the situation. (ANI)

stories.headline: AP Assessing Cyclone Damage: Relief and Rehabilitation to Continue
stories.title: AP Assessing Cyclone Damage: Relief and Rehabilitation to Continue
stories.summary: Meanwhile, the government will continue the relief and rehabilitation programme until assistance reaches the last affected person, said Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu while talking to reporters at Returu Village in Guntur district.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Meanwhile, the government will continue the relief and rehabilitation programme until assistance reaches the last affected person, said Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu while talking to reporters at Returu Village in Guntur district.
Andhra Pradesh government is assessing the damage caused by the two cyclones, Arnab and Murasu, which wreaked havoc within a gap of a couple of days, and would seek liberal central assistance.
He said extensive damage has been caused by the Murasu cyclone in Guntur, Bapatla and Prakasam.
Farmers suffered losses just when their crops were ready for harvest.

He said farmers had already faced difficult conditions due to El Nino but cultivated crops after receiving water through the Pattiseema project, adding that Cyclone Murasu struck when their crops were nearing harvest and expected to yield well.
Murasu crossed the coast on Tuesday between Nellore and Narsapur, near Ongole.
He said the government was seeking assistance from Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu for cyclone relief operations.
Around 30,000 electricity poles uprooted during Cyclone Arnab had been restored, while another 10,000 poles were damaged during Cyclone Murasu.
Electricity supply to aquaculture ponds was also being restored at the earliest.
The CM said precautionary measures taken by the government helped minimise property damage and enabled relief operations to be undertaken swiftly.
He urged people not to take cyclone warnings lightly when advance alerts were issued.

He further said the government was creating widespread awareness to ensure every farmer enrolled for crop insurance, adding that farmers could recover their lost investments through crop insurance and input subsidies.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Clarifies Judgment On OBC-Creamy Layer Parental Salary Computation
stories.title: Supreme Court Clarifies Judgment On OBC-Creamy Layer Parental Salary Computation
stories.summary: The Court stated that the jugment will not re-open already concluded selections and promotions.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 6) pronounced judgment on a Miscellaneous Application filed by the Centre seeking clarification of its March 11 judgment holding that the creamy layer status of an Other Backward Class (OBC) candidate cannot be determined solely on the basis of the parents' salary income, and that the category of posts held by them has also to be considered.
The Court clarified that the judgment was applicable to the parties before the Court and that seniority and promotions would not be reopened.
The pending cases will be decided by the courts on their own merits and entitlement.
The time to comply with the judgment was extended by eight weeks.
A bench of Justice Pamidighantam Sri Narasimha and Justice R. Mahadevan pronounced the judgment on a Miscellaneous Application filed by the Centre seeking prospective application of the judgment.
A copy of the judgment is awaited.

“Retrospective or belated application of a changed eligibility criterion may unsettle appointments and admissions made under the rules and certificates prevailing at the relevant time and may create uncertainty regarding OBC-NCL status, seniority, service conditions and career progression.
It may also affect admissions to Central and State educational institutions, universities and professional institutions.

The Applicant therefore respectfully submits that the temporal operation of the Judgment requires clarification so as to avoid unsettling completed selections, appointments and admissions and the consequential rights arising therefrom”, the plea states.

The Centre had sought two years to establish equivalence of posts in other organisations with government posts after consultations with the concerned stakeholders and to formulate a uniform mechanism for determining OBC creamy-layer status where equivalence has not been established.

The Centre had also sought permission to finalise service allocation for 958 candidates recommended by the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) in the Civil Services Examination (CSE) 2025, pending a decision on the clarification application.
By the March 11 judgment, the Supreme Court held that salary income alone cannot determine whether a candidate belongs to the OBC creamy layer.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Orders SIT Probe Into Illegal Gravel Mining In Rajasthan's Luni, Jojari And Bandi Rivers, Bars New Industries Near River Ecosystem
stories.title: Supreme Court Orders SIT Probe Into Illegal Gravel Mining In Rajasthan's Luni, Jojari And Bandi Rivers, Bars New Industries Near River Ecosystem
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has directed the Rajasthan government to constitute a Special Investigation Team (SIT) within three days to investigate organised illegal bajri (gravel) mining in the Luni, Jojari and Bandi rivers and their tributaries, including the involvement of public officials in facilitating such activities.

A bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta, in an order dated October 26, also restrained the State from granting permissions for the establishment of new industrial units along or in the vicinity of the riverine ecosystem until the High Flood Line and buffer zones are scientifically determined.
The SIT, to be headed by an officer not below the rank of Inspector General of Police, will include the Superintendents of Police of Jodhpur, Balotra and Pali.
“The SIT shall undertake a comprehensive investigation into organised illegal bajri mining activities affecting the Luni, Jojari and Bandi rivers and their tributaries.

The investigation shall extend to identifying the persons and entities involved in such activities, the networks through which the illegal extraction, transportation and sale of bajri are organised, and the beneficiaries of such operations”, the Court ordered.
The SIT also has to examine whether public officials facilitated or enabled illegal mining, including instances of collusion, dereliction of duty or failure to act despite knowledge of violations.
Appropriate action has to be initiated against those found responsible.
The Court directed the SIT to file a status report before it on or before the next date of hearing on 27th November, 2026.
The Court directed that an additional protective zone of 100 metres be maintained on either side of the respective recorded outer boundaries of the rivers.
The Court held that No Red Category industry shall be permitted to be established within a distance of 500 metres from the said recorded outer boundaries.

Observing that the issues involved in the present proceedings are complex and multifaceted in nature, the Court appointed Senior Advocate Balbir Singh along with Advocate on Record Namit Saxena as Amici Curiae to assist the Court in the effective consideration and resolution of the issues.

The Court passed the directions in the suo motu proceedings concerning pollution in the Jojari-Luni-Bandi river system, which has affected the environment and the lives of approximately 20 lakh people.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Dismisses Plea Challenging Allahabad HC's Senior Designations Conferred In 2019
stories.title: Supreme Court Dismisses Plea Challenging Allahabad HC's Senior Designations Conferred In 2019
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 6) dismissed a plea challenging senior advocate designations conferred by the Allahabad High Court in 2019.
A bench of Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe observed that the applicants who were not conferred the designation could apply afresh in the next round.
Advocate Pranav Sachdeva for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner was not considered despite having 15 years of unblemished continuous practice in Allahabad High Court.
However, Justice Narashimha questioned why he wanted to litigate the issue, responding, "Apply.
Why do you want to litigate?
You apply afresh.
Don't unnecessarily litigate."
Sachdeva alleged that the selection committee has not done the evaluation for several years despite the judgment in Jitendra Kalla.
State of NCT holding that at least one exercise of senior designation must be done every calendar year.
Ultimately, the Court ordered, "We are not inclined to interfere with the order passed by the High Court.

We make it clear that the petitioner will be entitled to reapply and upon such application it shall be considered in accordance with the law that governs the subject, including the principle laid down in Jitendra Kalla's case."
The Special Leave Petition was filed against the September 2024 judgment of the Allahabad High Court which rejected the petition filed by Advocate Vishnu Bihari Tiwari against the 2019 designations.

stories.headline: Supreme Court notice to KPCC office-bearers on contempt plea for social media post against CJI
stories.title: Supreme Court notice to KPCC office-bearers on contempt plea for social media post against CJI
stories.summary: A post against the CJI from the official X account of the Keralam unit of Congress went viral on October 12, drawing sharp criticism on social media, before it was deleted
reasons: rumour: 'went viral on' in summary (penalty 12.5, active)
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Noting that the judicial restraint is not an institutional weakness and attempts to undermine judicial authority will be dealt with an iron hand, the Supreme Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) sought responses from Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) office-bearers on a plea to initiate contempt proceedings against them for a social media post targeting Chief Justice of India Surya Kant.
The post was later deleted from the X account of the Indian National Congress Kerala unit.
KPCC president Sunny Joseph apologised for the post, saying it was unauthorised by the organisation and the act of one individual.
However, the apex court had registered a writ petition on the basis of a complaint filed by an advocate, Vineet Jindal.
On Friday (November 5, 2026), Justice Aravind Kumar, heading the Bench, asked if the apology rendered had indeed been heartfelt or just for the sake of form.
“The independence of the judiciary is not a matter of political convenience.
It is a Constitutional guarantee owed to the people of the Republic.
Judgments are always open to criticism, however severe.
But freedom of expression cannot become a shield of intimidation or interference with the administration of justice,” the Court remarked.
Justice Kumar said the authority of the Supreme Court did not require any political endorsement or approval.
The authority of the court and the administration of justice rested upon the Constitution and the rule of law.
